Definition: an epistle (as carried by a state courier or postman)
BiblicalUsage: A letter in Aramaic is how the enemies of the Jews tried to stop the temple. In Ezra 4:8 Rehum and Shimshai write a letter against Jerusalem, in Ezra 4:11 the copy of the letter is set out, and in Ezra 5:6 Tattenai writes another letter to Darius, asking whether the building should go on.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the letters tell the story plainly: men wrote to a king to stop God's house. God answered through a king's search of the records.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
